introduction: SSC and State PCS exams love to ask 'Hard Level' questions from the North-East (Seven Sisters). Memorizing these unique names and their associated states is the key to scoring high.

core_concepts.title: Festivals of Mizoram and Tripura
core_concepts.description:
1. **Chapchar Kut:** The biggest spring festival of **Mizoram**, celebrated after clearing the forests for 'Jhum' (shifting) cultivation. 
2. **Kharchi Puja:** A famous festival of **Tripura** that involves the worship of the 'Fourteen Gods' (Chaturdasha Devata).

core_concepts.title: Festivals of Meghalaya and Assam
core_concepts.description:
1. **Wangala:** Celebrated by the Garo tribe in **Meghalaya**. It is popularly known as the **'100 Drums Festival'**. It is a post-harvest festival dedicated to the Sun God (Saljong). 
2. **Bihu:** Celebrated 3 times a year in **Assam**: Rongali (Spring/New Year), Kongali (Autumn), and Bhogali (Winter Harvest).

core_concepts.title: Pushkar Fair and Sarhul
core_concepts.description:
1. **Pushkar Fair:** Held in Ajmer, **Rajasthan**. It is one of the world's largest camel fairs. The town also houses the only prominent temple dedicated to Lord Brahma in India. 
2. **Sarhul:** The most important spring festival of **Jharkhand** (celebrated by Oraon and Munda tribes). It translates to 'Worship of the Sal Tree', where nature is worshipped.

important_entities.name: Losar
important_entities.significance: Losar is a major Buddhist festival celebrated as the Tibetan New Year. In India, it is primarily celebrated in **Ladakh, Arunachal Pradesh, and Sikkim**.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: If you see a festival name ending with the word **'Kut'** (e.g., Chapchar Kut, Mim Kut, Thalfavang Kut), there is a 99% chance it belongs to **Mizoram**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Going on a 'Trip' (Tripura) requires 'Kharch' (Expense). Therefore, Kharchi Puja belongs to Tripura.

exam_strategy_tips: A favorite question in CGL/CPO: 'Which festival is also known as the 100 Drums Festival?' Answer: Wangala (Meghalaya).
